output.summary: KEP-2496 proposes etcdadm, a project combining Platform9's etcdadm CLI with kopeio's etcd-manager, to provide a common tool for etcd cluster creation, teardown, membership changes, backups, restores, upgrades, downgrades and PKI management for the Kubernetes control plane. Its current status is provisional.
output.rationale: Each installation tool reimplements etcd operation, which is difficult and leads to ecosystem fragmentation such as incompatible backups between tools. The proposal combines an imperative CLI base layer (etcdadm) with an automation layer (etcd-manager) that is rebased to call the CLI. The status is provisional, and the sources give no further rationale for the stage.

alternatives.option: Each installation tool keeps its own etcd operation code
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this approach is hard and leads to ecosystem fragmentation, e.g. backups from one tool are not necessarily compatible with others.

alternatives.option: Build a general-purpose etcd operation toolkit
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists as a non-goal: "We are not building a general-purpose etcd operation toolkit."

alternatives.option: Provide a full turn-up solution for etcd on clouds
alternatives.why_not: The readme says it is out of scope: "we aren't building a full 'turn up an etcd cluster on a cloud solution'; we expect this to be a building block".

evidence.quote: Today each installation tool must reimplement etcd operation, and this is difficult. It also leads to ecosystem fragmentation
We will combine the [etcdadm](https://github.com/platform9/etcdadm) from Platform9 with the [etcd-manager](https://github.com/kopeio/etcd-manager) project from kopeio
It will be rebased to work in terms of etcdadm CLI operations (which will likely require some functionality to be added to etcdadm itself).
we expect this to be a building block for use by kubernetes installation tooling (e.g. cluster API solutions).
